source: Tide experiment 2026-10-07; exact saved inputs, no transport or acceptance claim
brief: Build a simple responsive tide app. Let me choose a coastal location and day, see the tide height and whether it is rising or falling, the next high and low tides, and a readable 24-hour tide chart. Use the supplied data.

paragraph_context.content: Use the supplied React 19 / esbuild starter and unchanged public/data.js. The shared fixture contains 14 coastal locations and two dates. Measurements are metres and times Pacific time; the clock is noon on the selected day. Initial selection is Half Moon Bay, 2026-10-06. Every location/day must update all readings and the chart from the supplied values, with a chart scale that contains the selected data. Build and check with npm run build and npm run check. dist/index.html must work by file and local HTTP. Desktop 1280x800, mobile 390x844. Use local assets and system fonts; no live data APIs. Design decisions are delegated. Show light mode only with no system-theme switching. Do not add demo-data banners or notices. Keep units, timezone and selected-day clock clear. Output working code and RUN.md with resource calls, outcomes, QA, assumptions, and limitations. Standard file/shell/browser infrastructure is common to all conditions.

activity_model.activity: Check tides for a coastal outing.
activity_model.objective: Understand tide conditions for a chosen coastal location and day.
outcomes: Read noon height and direction, next high and low tides and the full day curve.
tools_and_artifacts: Supplied tide readings and daily events
rules_and_rituals: Use Pacific time and metres; reference noon on the chosen day.
division_of_labor: Person selects place and day; app calculates and presents supplied tide information.

interaction_contract.primary_decision: Which location and day to inspect?
next_actions: Compare upcoming high and low tides with the day curve
meaningful_state_changes: Location/day selection changes all measurements and chart scale together.
interaction_contract.completion: The person can read the selected day tide height, direction, upcoming events, and 24-hour pattern.
make_easy: Keep selections and resulting values visible together.

boundaries: Information from supplied values; no activity suitability decision is made.

assumptions.statement: Single informational view rather than an outing booking or safety decision.

work_units.label: Choose coastal location and day
work_units.purpose: Select one of the 14 coastal locations and one of the two days; initial selection Half Moon Bay, 2026-10-06.

work_units.label: Read tide at 12:00 noon Pacific time
work_units.purpose: Tide height in metres at the selected-day clock and whether the tide is rising or falling.

work_units.label: Read next high and next low
work_units.purpose: Time (Pacific time) and height (m) of the next high tide and next low tide after noon; an event at 24:00 is shown as 00:00 next day.

work_units.label: Scan the 24-hour tide chart
work_units.purpose: Hourly tide heights for the selected day with a scale that contains the selected data, the noon clock marked, and high/low points labelled.

workflow.completion_state: The person has read the noon height and direction, the next high and low, and the day curve for the chosen place and day; nothing is submitted or saved.

surface_set.name: Tide check
surface_set.purpose: Choose a coastal location and day, then read the noon tide height and direction, next high and low, and the 24-hour curve together.
sections: Place and day selection (coastal location, day)
Tide at 12:00 noon Pacific time (height in m, rising or falling)
Next high tide and next low tide (time Pacific time, height m)
24-hour tide trend chart (hourly heights, noon marker, high/low points, metre scale containing the day data)
Detailed high and low tide measurements for the day (table: tide, time Pacific time, height m)
surface_set.relationship_to_workflow: Read-only monitoring view: place/day selection sits above a summary (noon height and rising/falling signal), the next high/low signals, the 24-hour trend chart and a detailed measurements table; every change updates all of them together. Desktop 1280px two columns; mobile 390px one column, no horizontal overflow.

handoff.reason: Workflow covers selection, noon reading, next events and day chart for a read-only one-screen prototype.
handoff.next_action: Implement the Tide check workspace with the reviewed sections and states.
copy_rules: Use domain terms: coastal location, tide height, rising, falling, high tide, low tide, metres, Pacific time, noon
State units (m), timezone (Pacific time) and the selected-day clock (12:00 noon) visibly
No safety verdicts or outing recommendations; no demo-data banners; light mode only
handoff.data: Read-only supplied tide table; every reading and the chart update from supplied values on each selection.

assumptions: Surface recommendation (rerun, jk3/30) was workbench at low confidence with zero trigger scores; dashboard_monitor (track status, trends) is chosen because the completion state is reading a tide summary, direction signal, next extremes, trend chart and detailed measurements, with no decision or handoff action in this read-only check.
